Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

glasses3 (development version)

New features

  • g3_quality() summarises data quality per recording or epoch: the number of samples, the proportion with a gaze point and with data for each eye, and the longest time without a gaze point. It helps to find trials with too much missing data.
  • g3_add_frame() adds the number of the scene video frame shown at each sample, for matching samples to codes made from the video. g3_downsample() keeps the frame of the first sample in each bin.

Bug fixes

  • g3_fill_gaps() no longer fails on data with duplicated rows. The sampling rate, also shown by print() and summary(), is now worked out from the intervals between distinct timestamps. An infinite rate gives an error.
  • plot_g3_pupil() and plot_g3_gaze() no longer fail when some samples have no time, and summary() now gives the largest gap for such data.
  • A byte order mark at the start of a data file or of recording.g3 is ignored.
  • A damaged recording.g3 gives a clear error in read_g3_info() and read_g3(). list_g3_recordings() lists such recordings without metadata, with a warning, and the readers use the usual file names for them.
  • A data file that is a ZIP archive gives a clear error.
  • Columns of the wrong type, such as a time column holding text, give an error naming the column.
  • g3_add_clock_time() warns about recordings without a start time instead of returning NA without a warning.
  • g3_api_events() gives a clear error when the data column holds text that is not JSON, and is faster with many events.

glasses3 0.2.0

Breaking changes

  • The sync port functions g3_syncport(), g3_add_syncport(), g3_epochs() and plot_g3_pupil() now use direction = "in" by default, the pulses the glasses receive from other equipment such as a stimulus computer. Use direction = "out" for the pulses the glasses send.
  • g3_epochs() numbers the epochs in a new epoch column. Epochs cut at sync port pulses keep the pulse column with the pulse number. plot_g3_pupil(), g3_downsample() and g3_gaze_velocity() use epoch to keep epochs apart.

New features

  • g3_epochs() also cuts epochs at the onsets in a data frame with an onset column, such as the trial onsets of an experiment. Its other columns, such as a condition, are copied to the samples of each epoch. Without a recording column, every recording is cut at all onsets.
  • g3_api_events() extracts the events sent to the glasses through their API, with their tag and object, ready to be passed to g3_epochs().
  • g3_gaze_velocity() adds the angular velocity of each eye in degrees per second.
  • g3_add_clock_time() adds the date and time of each sample from the start time of the recording.
  • summary() of a recording counts the sync port pulses in both directions.

Bug fixes

  • g3_downsample() no longer splits a bin in two where a sync port pulse starts in data from g3_add_syncport(). The pulse column now gets the pulse of the first sample in the bin, and samples is an integer again.
  • A file in the meta folder that is not UTF-8 text, as the API can write, no longer stops read_g3_info(), read_g3() and list_g3_recordings(). Such files are returned as raw vectors, and folders inside meta are skipped.
  • Sync port signal changes without a value no longer create a pulse without an onset.
  • read_g3_gaze(), read_g3_imu() and read_g3_events() now take the names of the data files from recording.g3, as read_g3() already did.

Other changes

  • g3_downsample() is several times faster, and functions that work per recording are faster with many recordings.
  • Highlighted terms in the vignette and on the website are now shown with a highlighter.
  • The help page titles of g3_pupil_long() and list_g3_recordings() are now “Reshape pupil data to long format” and “List recordings”.

glasses3 0.1.0

  • Initial release.
  • Reads Tobii Pro Glasses 3 recording folders directly from the SD card: gaze and pupil data, IMU data, events and metadata. Lines that cannot be parsed, such as the cut-off last line of an incomplete file, are skipped with a warning. A file whose compressed data are damaged gives an error.
  • The readers accept several recording folders, or the output of list_g3_recordings(), and add a recording column. Sync port, epoch and plotting functions work per recording.
  • g3_syncport(), g3_add_syncport() and g3_epochs() align samples with sync port pulses, and g3_pupil_long() reshapes pupil data to one row per eye.
  • g3_fill_gaps() inserts empty rows for missing samples. The recording column and columns you added that have one value per recording, such as a participant column, are copied into the new rows.
  • g3_gaze_angles() adds azimuth, elevation and vergence angles.
  • g3_downsample() averages samples into fixed time bins, for example before fitting generalised additive mixed models. Its by argument keeps further grouping columns, such as participant or condition.
  • plot_g3_pupil() and plot_g3_gaze() share one style, available as theme_g3() for other plots. The left eye is always slate blue and the right eye always Indian red, a pair checked for colour vision deficiencies. Given epochs, plot_g3_pupil() plots the time from the pulse onset, with one line per pulse and the mean. Its smooth argument draws a running median over the raw trace.
  • Data are returned as tibbles, and grouped tibbles keep their groups. The internals use dplyr, tidyr, purrr and stringr.
  • Gaze, pupil, IMU and sync port data were checked against Tobii Pro Lab exports of seven 50 Hz recordings and agree up to the rounding of the exports. 100 Hz data are covered by synthetic test recordings.
  • citation("glasses3") gives the reference for the package, with the version number from DESCRIPTION.
